subject: Data Engineering
title: Stateful vs Stateless Processing
description: A quick, practical guide to Stateful vs Stateless Processing.

hook.text: Filtering events is easy — check a condition, pass or drop. But computing a running average? That needs memory.

buildup.text: Stateless processing handles each event independently. Stateful processing remembers past events.

discovery.text: Aggregations, joins, and deduplication all require state — stored counters, buffers, or lookup tables.

twist.text: State must survive crashes. If a node fails, its in-memory counters are lost unless checkpointed.

climax.text: Frameworks like Flink checkpoint state to durable storage, enabling recovery without data loss.

punchline.text: Stateless is simple. Stateful is powerful. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: Why is stateful stream processing more complex than stateless?
options: It must remember past events and survive crashes
It processes more events per second
